correctness.rationale: Every dyadic Kaczmarz frequency block is a reverse-bit Walsh transform of an affine digit weight. Orthogonality confines the block transform to zero and one-bit prefixes. For first two one-bits a<b the exact kernel numerator is 4^a-(2^a/3)(2*4^(b-a-1)+1); its negativity is equivalent to 3a<=2b-3. Counting 2^(n-b-1) cylinders and finite geometric sums yields all three formulas exactly. Fraction/integer checker independently passed 3786 assertions including direct transforms n=1..12, threshold through bit 84, finite sums n=1..60. The proof, not the samples, establishes the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The natural exact convergence rate to the sharp dyadic Walsh-Kaczmarz Fejér kernel bound has a surprising 2/3 exponent and three different sharp arithmetic phase constants. It quantifies finite-resolution operator amplification unavailable from a qualitative limit and exposes a precise binary-cylinder sign mechanism. This is a complete finite-index result for the canonical dyadic subsequence, not a routine index increment.
